title: vector chart values — tenant-isolation + evidence-channel trust roots
description: Constrains ONLY the two security-load-bearing blocks (tenantProjections = tenant isolation, evidenceChannel = the ADR-028 #1234 revocation-evidence PII gate); all other values are left unconstrained (additionalProperties defaults true). A quoted or non-integer accountId would otherwise render invalid VRL and only fail later at `vector validate`; this fails it at `helm template` with a clear message. Uniqueness of tenantId/accountId is enforced separately by a render-time {{ fail }} guard in templates/configmap.yaml (JSON Schema cannot express field-level cross-item uniqueness), as are the non-empty checks on evidenceChannel.events / .keepFields (deliberately NOT minItems here — the template's {{ fail }} explains WHY an empty list is a PII hole, and a bare schema error would replace that message).

evidenceChannel.description: ADR-028 D1 / #1234 federation revocation EVIDENCE channel — the pre-demux origin split plus the PII gate on the evidence branch. Constrained because a typo silently MISROUTES rather than failing: the split's two conditions are positive matches on a pod label, so a wrong podLabelValue matches nothing, every tenant-api row falls into the unconsumed origin_split._unmatched, and the channel is permanently empty and indistinguishable from 'no revocations happened'. A typo'd KEY (podLabelvalue, keepfields) is the case additionalProperties:false actually catches — the template would silently fall back to its shipped default. Nullable so `helm upgrade --reuse-values` / `--set evidenceChannel=null` (no such key in stored values) still renders; the template is nil-safe and defaults every field.

podLabelKey.description: Pod label key the origin split reads from the PRISTINE .kubernetes.pod_labels (default app.kubernetes.io/name). Must be a label both branches can be keyed on.

podLabelValue.description: Label value identifying the evidence producer (default tenant-api). MUST also be covered by source.extraLabelSelector or nothing is tailed at all. Distinctness from gatewayLabelValue is enforced by a render-time {{ fail }} (equal values would copy every row down BOTH branches — Vector's `route` fans out to every match).

gatewayLabelValue.description: Label value for the OTHER branch, the pre-existing audit pipeline feeding demux (default federation-gateway). A positive match on purpose: negation would make the split exhaustive and forward unrecognised rows into the 30-day 0:0 store.

podNamespace.description: #1288 producer binding: the namespace the evidence producer runs in (default tenant-api). Deliberately NO minLength — "" is the documented way to disable the binding and fall back to label-only matching, and the template distinguishes absent (take the default) from explicitly empty (disabled) via hasKey. A pod declares its own labels but cannot choose its namespace, so this is the only self-assignment-proof half of the origin split. A mismatch is bounded and loud: the heartbeat stops and FederationRevocationEvidenceChannelDown fires ~45-50 min after the last good heartbeat (30 min for it to age out of the 1800s canary window, up to one 300s reconcile interval, then the alert's for:15m).

gatewayNamespace.description: #1288 producer binding for the gateway branch (default monitoring). Same empty-disables semantics as podNamespace. ⚠️ A mismatch here is SILENT — FederationAuditPipelineSilent watches the mtail sidecar's own counters, a different path that stays green while the Vector side carries nothing. ⚠️ monitoring is a SHARED namespace, and a principal who can create pods there can reach VictoriaLogs :9428 directly (no auth, admits same-namespace pods by self-declared label — #1295), so this binding does not stop that actor; it closes the broader case of a labelled workload elsewhere in the cluster.

logType.description: Stream class stamped on evidence rows (default federation_evidence). Registered as a Tier-1 platform-only class in docs/internal/log-visibility-2tier-catalogue.md; changing it desynchronises that catalogue and the reconciler's LogsQL filter.

events.description: Fail-CLOSED ROW allowlist: the only `event` values that survive the evidence branch. Everything else aborts, which is what keeps tenant-api's per-request `caller` (operator EMAIL) / `remote` (client IP) out of the audit store. Adding an entry is a security-reviewed action. An explicitly empty list is rejected by a render-time {{ fail }}, not here.

keepFields.description: Fail-CLOSED FIELD keep-list (default: event, token_id, expires_at). The row is REBUILT from these keys, so anything unlisted is structurally absent. Widening it is a security-reviewed action — it is the second half of the PII gate, and it is the SSOT the log-visibility catalogue's evidence-row description tracks. An explicitly empty list is rejected by a render-time {{ fail }}, not here.

tenantProjections.description: Per-tenant log projection map — a reviewed, GitOps-versioned projection of the Git account registry.

tenantId.description: Must equal the federation-gateway audit JSON .tenant_id (the JWT claim).

accountId.description: The tenant's monotonic uint32 AccountID from _account_registry.yaml. >=1000 (0=platform, 1-999 reserved); must be quoted-free (a string makes the VRL route never match → silent empty partition).
